test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II (AAO) 2023 Official Paper-III (Held On: 27 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is regarded as a supervisory function of the Reserve Bank of India?

options.text: Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme

solution:
The correct answer is** Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Implementation of the deposit insurance scheme:**

 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) oversees the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC), which provides deposit insurance. This is a supervisory function to ensure the stability and safety of the banking system.
 
• The DICGC insures all bank deposits, such as savings, fixed, current, and recurring deposits, ensuring that depositors are protected in case of bank failures.
 
• This function is critical for maintaining public confidence in the banking system.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Banker to the government:**

 
 
• This is a key function of the RBI but not a supervisory function. The RBI manages the banking needs of the central and state governments, including managing their accounts and public debt.
 
 
 
• **Exchange rate management:**
 
 
• The RBI is responsible for managing the exchange rate of the Indian Rupee. It involves interventions in the foreign exchange market to stabilize the currency. However, this is not a supervisory function.
 
 
 
• **Issue of currency notes:**
 
 
• The RBI has the sole authority to issue currency notes in India. This function ensures the supply of adequate and quality currency notes but does not fall under the supervisory functions of the RBI.
